stemBlocks.value: Make l the subject of the formula T = 2π√(l/g) (the period of a simple pendulum).
Think first: l is buried under a square root inside a fraction, so free the root first and square only when it is alone.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p096-q13 from workbook page 96.

solutionSteps.instruction: Square both sides to remove the square root.
Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide by 2π to isolate the square root, square both sides, then multiply by g.

whyThisWorks.value: Squaring is the inverse of taking a square root, but it only cancels the root cleanly when the root stands alone on one side. Dividing by 2π first ensures that when you square, the 2π becomes 4π² correctly instead of being left half-processed inside the root.

commonErrors.misconception: Squaring straight away and writing T² = 2π²l/g, forgetting that (2π)² = 4π².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Squaring straight away and writing T² = 2π²l/g, forgetting that (2π)² = 4π².

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by 2 and π separately and mishandling the squaring.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by 2 and π separately and mishandling the squaring.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying by g before the root is removed.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying by g before the root is removed.

examTip.value: Isolate the radical before squaring — squaring both sides of an equation where the root is still attached to other factors is the single most common error in this topic.
